title: Extension by the empty set: adjunction with restriction, stalks, and j^{-1}j_! = id
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space (sheaves on $X$ are sheaves on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), $U\subseteq X$ an open subset, and let $j_{U,p!}$ and $j_{U!}$ be the extension by the empty set of presheaves and of sheaves of sets on $U$, with the sheafification $\theta_{\mathcal G}:j_{U,p!}\mathcal G\to j_{U!}\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], as in [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty] (the presheaf formula there makes sense, and is used below, for any presheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U$). For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on $X$ let $\mathcal P|_U$ be the presheaf on $U$ with $\mathcal P|_U(V)=\mathcal P(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ open and the restriction maps of $\mathcal P$, and for a morphism $\varphi$ let $\varphi|_U=(\varphi_V)_{V\subseteq U}$; if $\mathcal P$ is a sheaf, so is $\mathcal P|_U$ (this is the restriction $j_U^{-1}$). For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on a space $T$ and $t\in T$ let $\mathcal P_t=\varinjlim_{W\ni t}\mathcal P(W)$ be the stalk, the colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] over the open neighbourhoods of $t$ ordered by reverse inclusion, with germs $s\mapsto s_t$. Then:
(1) For every presheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U$ and every presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on $X$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G,\mathcal P)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal P|_U)$, $\psi\mapsto\psi|_U$ (note $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)|_U=\mathcal G$), is bijective, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal P$: the inverse sends $\alpha$ to $\tilde\alpha$ with $\tilde\alpha_V=\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and $\tilde\alpha_V$ the empty map $\emptyset\to\mathcal P(V)$ for $V\not\subseteq U$.
(2) For every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U$ and every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh(X)}(j_{U!}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh(U)}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F|_U)$, $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G})|_U$, is bijective, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$; the inverse sends $\alpha$ to the unique $\psi$ with $\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}=\tilde\alpha$ ($\tilde\alpha$ as in (1)). So $j_{U!}$ is left adjoint to $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F|_U$.
(3) For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U$ and $x\in X$: if $x\notin U$ then $(j_{U!}\mathcal G)_x=\emptyset$; if $x\in U$ then the map $\mathcal G_x\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G)_x$, $s_x\mapsto(\theta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$ ($V\subseteq U$ an open neighbourhood of $x$, $s\in\mathcal G(V)$), is well defined and bijective.
(4) $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)|_U=\mathcal G$ for every presheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U$, and for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $U$ the morphism $\theta_{\mathcal G}|_U:\mathcal G\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G)|_U$ is an isomorphism of sheaves on $U$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (restriction to $U$ of a sheaf is a sheaf).* Let $\mathcal P$ be a presheaf of sets on $X$. The rule $V\mapsto\mathcal P(V)$ ($V\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf $\mathcal P|_U$ on $U$, since the opens of $U$ are exactly the opens of $X$ contained in $U$ and the composition and identity laws are those of $\mathcal P$; for a morphism $\varphi$, $\varphi|_U=(\varphi_V)_{V\subseteq U}$ is natural for the same reason, and $(\gamma\circ\varphi)|_U=\gamma|_U\circ\varphi|_U$. A covering of $V\subseteq U$ in the site of open subsets of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is a family of opens $V_i\subseteq V$ with $\bigcup V_i=V$, which is also a covering of $V$ in the site of open subsets of $X$, with the same overlaps $V_i\cap V_k$ (the fibre products). So the equalizer diagram of the sheaf condition for $\mathcal P|_U$ and this covering is the one for $\mathcal P$ and the same covering; if $\mathcal P$ is a sheaf on $X$, $\mathcal P|_U$ is a sheaf on $U$. This is the claim inside the statement (Stacks 00A0 (2): 'clearly a sheaf').

proof.text:
*Step 2 (clause (1), and the first half of clause (4)).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf of sets on $U$. By the formula of [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty], $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$; so $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)|_U=\mathcal G$ as presheaves on $U$ (first half of (4)). Let $\mathcal P$ be a presheaf of sets on $X$. For $\psi:j_{U,p!}\mathcal G	o\mathcal P$, $\psi|_U:\mathcal G	o\mathcal P|_U$ is a morphism (Step 1). Conversely, for $\alpha:\mathcal G	o\mathcal P|_U$ put $	ilde\alpha_V=\alpha_V$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $	ilde\alpha_V=$ the empty map $\emptyset	o\mathcal P(V)$ if $V
ot\subseteq U$. Naturality of $	ilde\alpha$ for opens $V'\subseteq V$: if $V\subseteq U$ then $V'\subseteq U$ and it is the naturality of $\alpha$; if $V
ot\subseteq U$ both composites $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V)=\emptyset	o\mathcal P(V')$ are maps out of the empty set, hence equal. Clearly $	ilde\alpha|_U=\alpha$; and $\widetilde{\psi|_U}=\psi$, since both have the components $\psi_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and for $V

proof.text: *Step 3 (clause (2): the bijection).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $U$ and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of sets on $X$. Morphisms of sheaves are morphisms of the underlying presheaves, and by the universal property of the sheafification $\theta_{\mathcal G}:j_{U,p!}\mathcal G\to j_{U!}\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh(X)}(j_{U!}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$, $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}$, is bijective (every morphism from $j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ to the sheaf $\mathcal F$ factors uniquely through $\theta_{\mathcal G}$). Compose with the bijection $\varphi\mapsto\varphi|_U$ of Step 2 for $\mathcal P=\mathcal F$, onto $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F|_U)$, which is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh(U)}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F|_U)$ since $\mathcal F|_U$ is a sheaf (Step 1). The composite is $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G})|_U$, bijective, with inverse $\alpha\mapsto$ the unique $\psi$ with $\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}=\tilde\alpha$ (inverse of Step 2 followed by the inverse of the factorization).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00A3 (label lemma-j-shriek, line 4549), proof: 'The adjointness of $j_!$ and restriction follows from this and the properties of sheafification'

proof.text: *Step 4 (clause (2): naturality).* For $\beta:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of sheaves on $U$, $j_{U!}\beta$ is the morphism with $j_{U!}\beta\circ\theta_{\mathcal G'}=\theta_{\mathcal G}\circ j_{U,p!}\beta$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty]. For $\gamma:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ a morphism of sheaves on $X$ and $\psi:j_{U!}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$: $(\gamma\circ\psi\circ j_{U!}\beta\circ\theta_{\mathcal G'})|_U=(\gamma\circ\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}\circ j_{U,p!}\beta)|_U=\gamma|_U\circ(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G})|_U\circ\beta$, using $(j_{U,p!}\beta)|_U=\beta$ and Step 1. This is the naturality of the bijection of Step 3 in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$, so $j_{U!}$ is left adjoint to $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F|_U$ ('bifunctorially in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$').

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00A3 (label lemma-j-shriek, line 4549), proof; statement (2), 'bifunctorially'

proof.text:
*Step 5 (stalks of a restriction).* Let $\mathcal P$ be a presheaf of sets on $X$ and $x\in U$. The open neighbourhoods of $x$ in $X$, ordered by reverse inclusion, form a nonempty ($X
i x$) directed (two neighbourhoods $W,W'$ are both refined by $W\cap W'$) poset, hence a filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the same holds for the open neighbourhoods of $x$ in $U$, which are the neighbourhoods $W
i x$ of $X$ with $W\subseteq U$. The germs $\mathcal P(W)	o\mathcal P_x$ for $x\in W\subseteq U$ are compatible with restriction, so by the universal property of the colimit there is exactly one map $c:(\mathcal P|_U)_x	o\mathcal P_x$ sending the germ of $s\in\mathcal P(W)$ in $(\mathcal P|_U)_x$ to its germ in $\mathcal P_x$. It is bijective, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] for both colimits (a morphism $W	o W''$ of the index category means $W''\subseteq W$): surjective, since every element of $\mathcal P_x$ is $t_x$ for some open $W
i x$ and $t\in\mathcal P(W)$ (part (1)), and $t_x=(t|_{W\cap U})_x$ (the germs form a cocone) is $c$ of the germ of $t|_{W\cap U}$, as $x\in W\cap U\subseteq U$; injective, since two elements of $(\mathcal P|_U)_x$ are germs of some $s\in\mathcal P(W)$, $s'\in\mathcal P(W')$ with $W,W'\subseteq U$ (part (1)), and if their images in $\mathcal P_x$ agree, part (2) gives an open $W''
i x$ with $W''\subseteq W\cap W'$ and $s|_{W''}=s'|_{W''}$; then $W''\subseteq U$, so by part (2) again (the converse direction, for the colimit over the neighbourhoods in $U$) the two germs in $(\mathcal P|_U)_x$ agree. (Stacks 00A0 (3): 'the collection of open neighbourhoods of $u$ which are contained in $U$ is cofinal'.)

proof.text: *Step 6 (clause (3), $x\notin U$).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $U$ and $x\in X\setminus U$. Every open neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ satisfies $W\not\subseteq U$, so $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(W)=\emptyset$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty]. The index category of the stalk is filtered (Step 5), and by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1) every element of $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)_x$ is the germ of an element of some $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(W)=\emptyset$; so $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)_x=\emptyset$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-stalk-sheafification-space] applied to $\mathcal P=j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ and its sheafification $\theta_{\mathcal G}$, the map $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)_x\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G)_x$ is bijective, so $(j_{U!}\mathcal G)_x=\emptyset$.

proof.text: *Step 7 (clause (3), $x\in U$).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $U$ and $x\in U$. The stalk $\mathcal G_x$ (colimit over the open neighbourhoods $V$ of $x$ in $U$) is the stalk at $x$ of $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)|_U=\mathcal G$ (Step 2). Step 5 for $\mathcal P=j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ gives the bijection $\kappa:\mathcal G_x\to(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)_x$, $s_x\mapsto s_x$ ($s\in\mathcal G(V)=(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V)$, $x\in V\subseteq U$). [lem-weil-pbc-sets-stalk-sheafification-space] for $\mathcal P=j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ gives the bijection $\theta_{\mathcal G,x}:(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)_x\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G)_x$, $s_x\mapsto(\theta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$. The composite $\theta_{\mathcal G,x}\circ\kappa$ is bijective and sends $s_x$ to $(\theta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$ for every open $V$ with $x\in V\subseteq U$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(V)$. So the map of clause (3) is well defined (it is this composite; its value on $s_x$ does not depend on the representative $(V,s)$) and bijective.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00A3 (label lemma-j-shriek, line 4549), proof, stalk identification; Lemma Tag 00A0 (3) and Lemma Tag 007Z (lemma-stalk-sheafification)

proof.text: *Step 8 (clause (4), second half).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $U$. By Steps 1 and 2, $\theta_{\mathcal G}|_U$ is a morphism from $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)|_U=\mathcal G$ to $(j_{U!}\mathcal G)|_U$, and both are sheaves of sets on the space $U$ ($j_{U!}\mathcal G$ is a sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty], so Step 1 applies). Let $x\in U$. The stalk map $(\theta_{\mathcal G}|_U)_x:\mathcal G_x\to((j_{U!}\mathcal G)|_U)_x$ sends $s_x$ to the germ of $\theta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)$ in $((j_{U!}\mathcal G)|_U)_x$; following it by the bijection $c:((j_{U!}\mathcal G)|_U)_x\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G)_x$ of Step 5 (for $\mathcal P=j_{U!}\mathcal G$) gives $s_x\mapsto(\theta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$, which is the bijection of Step 7. So $(\theta_{\mathcal G}|_U)_x=c^{-1}\circ(\text{the map of Step 7})$ is bijective for every $x\in U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks], applied on the topological space $U$, $\theta_{\mathcal G}|_U$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets on $U$. (Stacks proves (4) and (5) 'by computing the value of the sheaf on any open of $U$'; that computation needs a description of the sections of a sheafification which no node states, so the step goes through the stalks of Step 7 and the criterion of Lemma Tag 007T (3) instead.)
